solutions.check: bars rebuilt from the blog's numbered answers (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Heard storyteller getting a stringed instrument

indicators.note: what is heard is spoken, so the word is taken by its sound, not its spelling

blocks.note: a storyteller in the sense of one who tells lies

explanation.surface: A bard who tells tales picks up a harp to accompany himself.
explanation.definitionFit: The small harp of ancient Greece is the classic stringed instrument of poets and minstrels.

clue.text: Bargeman clearing river dregs

indicators.note: clearing something away removes it, so the river's letter is taken out

blocks.note: a legger propelled a barge through a canal tunnel by walking his feet along the walls
R is the usual abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: A canal worker dredges the sludge out of a river.
explanation.walkthrough: LEGGER loses its R. The answer is an old word found in Chambers, a dictionary Mephisto solvers rely on.
explanation.definitionFit: An obsolete word for sediment or lees, the worthless remainder at the bottom of a vessel.

clue.text: Derby side needing energy at full speed up north

indicators.note: needing something means being without it, so the energy letter is missing

blocks.note: Derby County football club are nicknamed the Rams
a side is a team
E is the symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A football team from Derby is told it needs more energy if it is to go full pelt in the north.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Derby side' looks like one unit, the club, but it splits: Derby gives the nickname and side gives TEAM, which loses its E.
explanation.definitionFit: A Scots word meaning headlong or in reckless haste, hence 'up north'.

clue.text: Mephistopheleans can't do without this Greek city!

indicators.note: a word that cannot do without something must contain it, so the letters sit inside

blocks.note: found in the middle of the word, between PH and NS

explanation.surface: A joke that Mephisto devotees cannot manage without some Greek town.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue plays on the solvers of this very series; the city sits inside their name.
explanation.definitionFit: An ancient Greek colony in southern Italy, home of the Eleatic philosophers Parmenides and Zeno.

clue.text: Cuts coming from Man C and Man U?

definitions.text: Cuts coming from Man C and Man U?

blocks.note: surface reading: pieces of meat butchered from some beast
setter's reading: Manchester City and Manchester United, two leading football clubs of the Premier League

explanation.walkthrough: Man C and Man U are shorthand for the two Manchester football clubs; as the best teams they are the leading sides, and that phrase is also a joint of beef.
explanation.definitionFit: The joint cut from the upper part of a leg of beef is the familiar roasting cut sold under this name.

clue.text: Tesla sadly in Samoa smash

blocks.note: T is the symbol for the tesla, the unit of magnetic flux density
alas is said sadly

explanation.surface: A Tesla car comes to grief in a crash on a Pacific island.
explanation.walkthrough: Tesla looks like the car maker, but it is the physics unit. Smash is slang for money, and the tala is Samoa's currency.
explanation.definitionFit: The tala is the currency unit of Samoa, so several of them are the islanders' cash.

clue.text: Single last letter in US spoken of for leisurewear

indicators.note: something spoken of is said aloud, so the letter's name is used for its sound

blocks.note: single means one
Americans call the final letter of the alphabet zee

explanation.surface: An American lecturer remarks on how the alphabet's final letter is pronounced.
explanation.definitionFit: A one-piece all-in-one garment worn for lounging about at home, a modern sort of casual clothing.

clue.text: Fog in the London area after warming up

indicators.note: a body warming up loosens and moves about, so these letters are shaken into a new order

blocks.note: London lies in the South East of England
taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: Mist lingers over London once the day starts to get warmer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fog in the London area' reads as one phrase; only the first word defines.
explanation.definitionFit: A sea fret is a cold mist that rolls in off the sea onto England's east coast.

clue.text: Sibelius was one keen to scrap introductions as a false formality?

indicators.note: an introduction is a beginning, so scrapping them removes each word's opening letter

blocks.note: the composer Jean Sibelius was from Finland
game means willing or keen

explanation.surface: A puzzled query about whether Sibelius wanted to dispense with formal introductions.
explanation.walkthrough: Sibelius looks like a cue for music, but the clue wants his nationality. Game in the sense of willing is an everyday British usage.
explanation.definitionFit: Something done in name only is nominal: an empty formality, not the real thing.

clue.text: Shift work texted omitting double time and inept

indicators.note: to work material is to knead and reshape it, so the letters are reformed
omitting means leaving out, so the two time letters are dropped

blocks.note: taken as written
T is the abbreviation for time, doubled
taken as written

explanation.surface: A clumsy text message about overtime is sent by someone not up to the job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shift work' looks like a phrase about rotas; shift is the definition and work the signal. TEXTED loses both its Ts.
explanation.definitionFit: A shift in the sense of a contrivance or makeshift means is an expedient, a noun here.

clue.text: Some plants in coniferous woods, we hear

indicators.note: what we hear is spoken, so the phrase is taken by sound alone

blocks.note: cedars are coniferous trees, and their timber is cedar wood

explanation.surface: Certain plants are reported to grow among the pine forests.
explanation.definitionFit: Plants that produce or shed seed, the botanical sense, so only certain ones qualify.

clue.text: Line manager briefly ordered change in Eswatini

indicators.note: putting something briefly cuts it short, so the final letter goes
ordered means arranged anew, so the letters are put in a fresh sequence

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written, then shortened

explanation.surface: A boss tersely instructs staff to make changes at an African office.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Change' looks like the anagram signal, but it means small money. Eswatini is the country formerly called Swaziland.
explanation.definitionFit: Emalangeni is the plural of lilangeni, the currency unit of Eswatini, so it is that country's cash.

clue.text: Ring back on catching British artist in shot

indicators.note: going back means running the word from end to start
shot here means got rid of, so the word in goes from the artist's name
catching something means holding it inside, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: in cricket the on side is also called the leg side
Tracey Emin, the British artist

explanation.surface: A photographer has a famous British artist return to a ring for a picture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in shot' sounds like being photographed; actually the letters IN are shot from Tracey Emin's surname, leaving EM.
explanation.definitionFit: A gemel, or gimmal, is a ring made of two interlocking hoops, so a kind of finger ring.

clue.text: What you sit on with a soft base?

definitions.text: What you sit on with a soft base?

blocks.note: can is slang, chiefly American, for the buttocks
taken as written
P is piano, soft in music
e is the base of natural logarithms

explanation.surface: A riddle about a comfy seat with a well-padded bottom.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue describes a sofa, which the French word also means; the same words build the answer piece by piece.
explanation.definitionFit: In French and in older English use a canapé is a sofa, a seat with a soft padded base.

clue.text: Contrary to reports, worker's at home on French river

blocks.note: the worker ant is the crossword's stock worker
someone at home is in
the Oise flows through northern France into the Seine

explanation.surface: Despite what is said, a labourer is relaxing at home on a river in France.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Contrary to reports' looks like 'despite what was said'; reports here are loud bangs.
explanation.definitionFit: Anti-noise means opposed to loud sound, and reports are bangs such as gunshots.

clue.text: Sleeper in Washington great penetrating secret service department

indicators.note: something penetrating goes into another thing, so this piece sits inside

blocks.note: the Special Operations Executive, Britain's secret wartime organisation
fab, short for fabulous, means great
D is the abbreviation for department

explanation.surface: A spy story: an American sleeper agent infiltrates a British secret service unit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sleeper' suggests a mole; it is a fold-out bed, and Americans call such a couch a sleeper.
explanation.definitionFit: In the US a sleeper, or sleeper sofa, is a couch that unfolds into a bed for guests.

clue.text: Concealed in confinement, a sister's small bulge

indicators.note: something concealed in other words sits inside them, ready to be found

blocks.note: running across the end of confinement into a sister's

explanation.surface: A nurse notices a pregnant sister's growing bump during her confinement.
explanation.walkthrough: Confinement is the old word for the late stage of pregnancy, which colours 'small bulge'.
explanation.definitionFit: The architectural term for the slight convex swelling given to a column's shaft to correct an optical illusion.

clue.text: Kind and unassuming saint coming unstuck

indicators.note: something that comes unstuck falls away, so the saint's letters drop off

blocks.note: unassuming means modest
St is the abbreviation for saint

explanation.surface: A gentle, humble holy figure suffers a breakdown.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kind and unassuming' reads as a pair of adjectives; kind is a noun meaning sort.
explanation.definitionFit: A mode is a way or manner, so a sort or variety of something.

clue.text: Career impressed head of employment

indicators.note: the head of a word is its opening letter

blocks.note: a seal stamped on wax is impressed
its first letter

explanation.surface: A career advisor is struck by the boss of a recruitment agency.
explanation.walkthrough: Career looks like a job; it is the verb, meaning rush along wildly.
explanation.definitionFit: To career is to dash headlong, as a frightened herd does in a mass rush.

clue.text: Sort of plant needing sun picked out

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for sun
a plant grown in a pot is a potted one

explanation.surface: A gardener says a type of houseplant needs sunshine and should be selected.
explanation.definitionFit: To spot something is to notice or pick it out from its surroundings, so picked out is a synonym.

clue.text: A very long time to get part for fiddlers?

blocks.note: per means a, as in so much per day
an aeon is an age

explanation.surface: An orchestral player waits ages to be given a role.
explanation.walkthrough: Fiddlers sound like violinists; they are fiddler crabs.
explanation.definitionFit: The peraeon is the thorax of a crustacean, the body section bearing the walking legs.

clue.text: Stick around Greek island — it's sweet

indicators.note: around means surrounding, so one piece wraps the other

blocks.note: to stick is to glue
Kos, or Cos, is a Greek island in the Dodecanese

explanation.surface: Someone on holiday is told to hang around a Greek island because it is lovely.
explanation.definitionFit: A simple sugar, dextrose, found in fruit and honey and in the blood.

clue.text: Shirt present right away causing a laugh

indicators.note: something sent away is gone, so that letter is dropped

blocks.note: a tee is a T-shirt
present at a roll call means here
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A T-shirt given as a gift turns out to be a joke.
explanation.definitionFit: A tittering giggle; the word imitates a high-pitched suppressed snigger.

clue.text: Colonnades in designs from Brussels?

blocks.note: Brussels is the seat of the European Union
styles are designs

explanation.surface: Columned walkways built to designs approved by Eurocrats.
explanation.definitionFit: A eustyle is a colonnade with columns spaced at the classically ideal interval of two and a quarter diameters.

clue.text: Indian committee is about keeping a lot of friendship

indicators.note: about means turned round, so the little word runs backwards
a lot of something is most but not all of it, so the final letter goes
keeping something means holding it within

blocks.note: taken as written
amity is friendship

explanation.surface: A committee in India is said to be all about fostering goodwill.
explanation.definitionFit: A Hindi word for an association or committee, used for co-operative and political bodies in India.

clue.text: In short as before head's beginning to drop off

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter, and dropping off loses it

blocks.note: bonce is British slang for the head

explanation.surface: Briefly put, a man is nodding off just as he was earlier.
explanation.walkthrough: BONCE loses its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Once means formerly, at some earlier time, which is how things were previously.

clue.text: The old claw back facilities associated with relative

indicators.note: going back means running the word from end to start

blocks.note: lats, short for latrines, are toilet facilities
an aunt is a relative

explanation.surface: An elderly person recovers the use of the lavatories through a family connection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Facilities' is the euphemism for toilets; a lat is an army latrine.
explanation.definitionFit: An obsolete form of talon, the hooked claw of a bird of prey, as 'The old' signals.

clue.text: Woman left union with people of intelligence

blocks.note: L is the abbreviation for left
U is the abbreviation for union
the Central Intelligence Agency, America's spy service

explanation.surface: A woman abandoned her marriage to join a group of spies.
explanation.definitionFit: Lucia is a female given name, so it can stand for a woman in crossword terms.

clue.text: Our special is ham

blocks.note: the newspaper's own word for itself, as in The Times
SP is an abbreviation for special

explanation.surface: A restaurant menu boasts that today's special dish is gammon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ham' looks like a food; it is an overacting performer.
explanation.definitionFit: A ham is a bad, overacting actor, and a thesp, short for thespian, is any actor.

clue.text: Ornate piece of material developed for needle holder

indicators.note: a piece of a word here is just its opening letter
developed means worked into a new form, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
its first letter

explanation.surface: A seamstress works up a fancy bit of fabric to make a pincushion.
explanation.walkthrough: The needle is a gramophone stylus, not a sewing needle.
explanation.definitionFit: The pivoting arm of a record player carries the stylus, the needle that tracks the groove.

clue.text: Short warning is needed for a crop retardant

indicators.note: a word cut short loses its final letter

blocks.note: an alarm is a warning

explanation.surface: A brief warning must accompany a chemical sprayed on crops.
explanation.definitionFit: The trade name of daminozide, a plant growth regulator once sprayed on apples to slow growth.

clue.text: Little people appearing in miscellanies out of step

indicators.note: taking something out of a word leaves it without those letters

blocks.note: pastiches are medleys made of borrowed pieces
pas is the French and ballet word for a step

explanation.surface: Small folk turn up in assorted collections but cannot keep in time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Out of step' reads as an idiom for marching wrongly; it splits into the deletion signal and the dance step. A tich, or titch, is British slang for a small person.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang for small persons, from the music-hall comedian Little Tich.

clue.text: Glenn's encounter in Shakespeare

blocks.note: first meaning: the surname of the American actress Glenn of Fatal Attraction
second meaning: in Shakespeare's usage a grapple or bout in fighting

explanation.surface: An actress named Glenn meets someone in a Shakespeare play.
explanation.walkthrough: Glenn looks like a man's name; it is the actress Glenn Close.
explanation.definitionFit: The actress's surname, and an old noun for a hand-to-hand fight or grapple used by Shakespeare.

clue.text: Liaison set up leading to serious complaint

indicators.note: something set up has been broken and put together differently, so the letters are mixed

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An affair, once arranged, leads to grave trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set up' reads as arranging an affair; up alone is the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A rare disease in which overgrowth of the facial bones gives a lion-like face, a grave medical disorder.

clue.text: Crack and ecstasy with time bringing on this?

definitions.text: Crack and ecstasy with time bringing on this?

indicators.note: to crack something is to break it apart so its letters can be reassembled

blocks.note: taken as written
E is slang for the drug ecstasy
taken as written

explanation.surface: A warning that taking hard drugs over the years may lead to mental decline.
explanation.walkthrough: Crack and ecstasy read as two drugs; crack is the signal, and the whole clue suggests what drugs plus age may bring on.
explanation.definitionFit: Dementia is a decline of memory and reasoning, which age and drug abuse can both cause.

clue.text: Talk about tree finally cut down

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one piece goes round the other
finally points to the last letter of the word

blocks.note: to rap is to talk, as in a rap session
its last letter

explanation.surface: A discussion about a tree that ends up being felled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut down' reads as felling the tree; it is the definition, harvesting a crop.
explanation.definitionFit: To reap is to cut down a crop such as grain with a scythe or sickle at harvest.
